name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v2176: A different model family reviewed v2175 and found eight things, six of them real, and the best one was architectural: the hunt memory keyed on a HASH compared with equality, and equality is the wrong question. What a paid retry has to answer is whether there is MORE film to search than when it last paid, and a hash can only say whether something is different. Different is not more. Archiving a reel changed the hash, so every remembered name was bought again to search strictly LESS footage, and removing footage can never turn a miss into a hit. One reel whose listdir stumbled read minus one instead of eighteen and moved the hash the same way. The memory now stores a LEVEL, total frames plus the newest frame time, and a name is re-hunted only when that level RISES. Five more from the same review are fixed with it. A fingerprint we FAILED to take was stored as null and compared with null, which is true, so an unknown granted a permanent skip. A name the hunt answered for with an empty list was filed as never-found because the test was falsiness rather than absence. A whole-file write lost the entire memory when a crash left partial JSON or when a second sweep overwrote the first, which is the shape that erased pt signals every seventeen seconds, so it now merges and replaces atomically. The failure path returned over the save, discarding empties already paid for. The file grew forever because the timestamp was written and never read, and it is the pruning key now. And the eagle check itself carried the threshold-above-the-ceiling scar: one real pass of the loop it watches is 144 reads and its floor was 200, so nothing could fire until the loop had paid twice, while an unparsable log line returned a confident green. It pins the law instead: two passes home empty is the loop, at any price.
